text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 3170002468 — elevated 5xx rate on streaming gateway routes detected by anomaly detector (metric: gateway.streaming.5xx_rate). paging eng-oncall. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-5xx

oncall-bot: severity: P1 if client-visible streaming disconnects > 1% and persists > 10m. channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall, #support.

mike: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs and SLO dashboard now.

alex: saw the spike around 2026-03-15T02:14Z, 5xx jumped from 0.2% -> 3.4% on streaming fanout endpoints. latency also increased 95th -> 750ms.

sara: pasting a few nginx/gateway snippets — looks like chunked encoding truncation + upstream EOFs:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:11Z gateway-1 nginx: [error] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.4.5.6, server: streaming.redwood, request: "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://pod-abc:8080/stream", host: "streaming.redwood"
2026-03-15T02:14:12Z pod-abc app: error during chunked write: unexpected EOF while writing chunked frame
2026-03-15T02:15:02Z gateway-2 nginx: [crit] upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```

mike: that matches customer reports — Support triage showing ~12 customers with errors in last 15m, some aborted sessions. cs-ops: can you confirm impacted accounts and prioritize notifications?

cs-ops: Confirmed: AGILEHealth, ScribeX, KraneAI are showing increased error volume and some canceled streams. CS will notify AGILEHealth and KraneAI immediately; ScribeX has a high-volume job so we're leaning emergency comms.

alex: quick repro via curl shows streaming stream dies after a few chunks with 502: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/stream -d '{"model":"x-large","input":"long prompt..."}' -v
# response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
# truncated chunked body, then connection reset
```

sara: probable root causes to check in parallel: kernel epoll backlog on gateway nodes, abrupt worker OOMs in runtime, or a regression in chunked encoder after last runtime release.

mike: quick mitigations to reduce customer impact while we triage:
- enable paged fallback for streaming routes for affected customers (non-streaming, polled pages)
- increase gateway proxy timeout/keepalive for streaming temporarily from 30s -> 120s
- scale gateway replicas and bump workers on pod groups showing epoll backlog
- enable extra logging on streaming gateway to capture chunk boundaries

alex: I'm flipping on paged fallback for the tenant routing rule for KraneAI and AGILEHealth now. command: 
```bash
redwoodctl route update --tenant kraneai --streaming-fallback paged --duration 30m --reason "live mitigation 5xx spike"
```

sara: I can change nginx upstream read_timeout and keepalive in the gateway config to 120s for the affected AZ. Pushing a canary on two nodes first.

mike: also let's add a temporary gateway feature-flag to force single-connection fanout (reduces simultaneous upstream connections) — reduces fanout pressure. alex, can you apply?

alex: applying FF: 
```bash
kubectl -n gateway set env deploy/gateway FEATURE_SINGLE_FANOUT=true
# will roll pods, doing 2x at a time for canary
```

oncall-bot: NOTE: please record mitigation steps in incident doc and tag with incident id 3170002468.

cs-ops: Notifying account teams now. Holding off on external status page until we have a clearer RCA window.

mike: checking runtime pods — a few runtime instances logged 'premature stream close' and then restarted (OOM kill). collecting heap profiles and core dumps. sara, can you check kernel logs for epoll/nf_conntrack exhaustion?

sara: already on it. seeing elevated epoll waitqueue lengths on gateway-2; sysctl net.core.somaxconn looks default (128) — bumping to 512 on nodes that are under pressure via daemonset for node config: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system create configmap node-tuning --from-literal=somaxconn=512 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# then rolling restart of gateway node agent to apply
```

alex: first mitigation results: after enabling paged fallback for two tenants and the FF, 5xx rate for those tenants dropped to ~0.4% within 6 minutes. overall cluster 5xx rate reduced from 3.4% -> 1.1%.

mike: great. still seeing intermittent disconnects for the larger demo workloads (ScribeX). plan: continue scaling gateway and identify offending runtime pod. if we confirm a runtime regression, prepare a rollback to previous runtime build.

sara: I found one runtime pod with a high RSS and many goroutine stacks blocked on chunk writer. capturing stack and will attach to the incident doc.

mike: CS/Acct teams: please escalate ScribeX - ask them to pause any burst ingestion jobs for 30 minutes while we stabilize.

cs-ops: done. ScribeX responded and paused ingestion; they appreciate the heads up.

oncall-bot: Escalation rules: if customer-impacting errors persist > 30m after mitigation, escalate to Eng-SRE and Director oncall. Timer started.

alex: just pushed a hotfix candidate to a small canary subset that reverts the chunked encoder change from the last runtime release. canary running on 3 pods. monitoring.

mike: while canary runs, let's keep paged fallback for the high-volume tenants. Also add a temporary rate-limit for unauthenticated demo traffic to reduce noise: 
```bash
redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope demo --rps 5 --duration 1h --reason "reduce demo noise during incident"
```

sara: canary looks promising — no chunked truncation on canary pods for the last 12 minutes. metrics show canary pods 0% 5xx. rolling patch to remaining runtime pods in the cluster over next 10m.

mike: rolling patch in progress. will monitor 5xx and streaming disconnects.

alex: patched. gateway 5xx rate dropped cluster-wide to 0.3% and customer errors are trending down. removing paged fallback for KraneAI and AGILEHealth in 15m if stable.

cs-ops: preparing post-incident comms for impacted customers: summary, timeline, mitigation steps, and next steps (follow-up RCA). tagging support tickets.

mike: starting incident timeline and impact summary now. key action items:
- collect heap/stack dumps and attach to RCA (sara)
- node-tuning changes and justification (alex)
- runtime regression delta and commit id for revert (mike)
- customer notif drafts (cs-ops)

oncall-bot: incident timer: 18m elapsed. current severity downgraded to P2 (customer impact reducing).

mike: handing off to taylor for overnight oncall. I have runbook notes and links in the incident doc. taylor, summarize state and next checks:
- confirm no new 5xx spikes in next 30m
- verify ScribeX paused ingestion and re-enable only after green for 60m
- ensure paged fallback removed for tenants if stable
- follow up on RCA artifacts (heap/profile)

taylor: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and will escalate if errors creep up. thanks team. leaving short checklist in the incident doc and adding ownership tags.

mike: thanks all — great coordination. closing live mitigation phase. will reopen incident doc for RCA write-up.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT 3170002468 — mitigation complete. record final status and transitions: mitigations applied: paged-fallback, kernel somaxconn bump, runtime revert canary -> global, gateway feature-flag single-fanout, temporary rate-limits. handoff to taylor.

taylor: noted. I'll file the RCA tomorrow and schedule a postmortem with Eng/Runtime/SRE.
